title: US Bitcoin ETFs lose $582 million on November 19 as BlackRock leads redemptions
description: US spot Bitcoin funds recorded roughly $582 million in net withdrawals on November 19, with BlackRock's IBIT accounting for $541.1 million while Morgan Stanley's MSBT attracted new money.
why_it_matters: The sharp divergence between IBIT redemptions and MSBT inflows shows that aggregate Bitcoin ETF flows can obscure fund-level differences. November's cumulative withdrawals also highlight pressure on regulated crypto investment products.
keyTakeaways: Farside Investors recorded approximately $582.3 million in net US spot Bitcoin ETF outflows on November 19.
BlackRock's IBIT accounted for $541.1 million in redemptions, while Morgan Stanley's MSBT received $49.6 million.
The Block reported roughly $3.47 billion in cumulative November outflows through November 19.
body:
US-listed spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds registered approximately $582.3 million in net outflows on November 19, 2026, according to the daily fund-level table published by Farside Investors. The result marked a third consecutive negative trading session, following roughly $239.9 million in withdrawals on November 17 and $306.5 million on November 18.

BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust, or IBIT, accounted for $541.1 million of the November 19 net withdrawals. Fidelity's FBTC lost $45.9 million, Ark 21Shares' ARKB lost $31.3 million and Grayscale's GBTC lost $13.9 million. The pattern was not universal: Morgan Stanley's MSBT attracted $49.6 million, while WisdomTree's BTCW added about $0.3 million, according to Farside's table.

The Block reported that cumulative November net outflows had reached approximately $3.47 billion through November 19. That is a flow measure, not a measure of Bitcoin price losses or proof that every ETF holder sold. Differences between individual funds are important when assessing demand for listed Bitcoin exposure.

facts.claim: Farside Investors lists net withdrawals of approximately 582.3 million dollars across US spot Bitcoin ETFs on November 19.
The November 19 fund-level table reports BlackRock IBIT net outflows of 541.1 million dollars.
Morgan Stanley MSBT registered 49.6 million dollars in net inflows on November 19.
The Block reports cumulative November ETF net withdrawals of approximately 3.47 billion dollars.
The Block identifies November 19 as the third consecutive negative trading session for US spot Bitcoin ETFs.
facts.anchor: third straight day of net outflows
